rationale: Round 0 built and ran cleanly, so the table shifts toward stronger obfuscation: SUB stays near-universal (negligible cost, applied to all 32 small functions for a broad baseline of altered arithmetic), and FLA gets the highest SecurityGain since testA/testB/testC and the step functions are loop-driven and benefit most from control-flow flattening, while its CorrectnessRisk stays moderate to protect the array-step invariants. BCF is applied selectively (SecurityGain 0.75 with higher SizeCost weight 0.45) because the binary is only 1266 text bytes and bogus-control-flow expansion on such small functions consumes the size budget quickly. SPLIT is kept as a cheap diversity amplifier that composes with FLA, IBR and ICALL get elevated weights to add indirection-based resistance in a program whose hot loops are simple enough that modest indirect-dispatch overhead is tolerable, and IGV is included but capped with the highest CorrectnessRisk weight (0.3) since global-variable indirection most often breaks pointer/aliasing assumptions in array-walking code like initarray and stepA/B/C. Cost weights remain below the security weights everywhere so the selector biases toward application, but they are high enough on BCF/IBR/IGV to keep those passes off the hottest inner-loop functions if the feature profile flags high runtime sensitivity.
